title: Your guide to Mesquite: Things to do, restaurants, parks and more - NewsBreak
text:
By José Sánchez Córdova ,
15 hours ago View of the Mesquite Rodeo buildings. (Tom Fox/Staff Photographer) Just east of Dallas, you’ll find Mesquite , the official Rodeo Capital of Texas.
Home to the historic Mesquite Championship Rodeo, the city also features a growing downtown district and a variety of entertainment and dining options.
Here’s your guide to Mesquite:

Compiled by staff researcher Rachel Friend. Data from U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 1-Year Estimates Subject Tables, Tables S0601, S1501, S1903, S2301, DP04.
A brief history Mesquite was founded in 1873 as a depot town for the Texas and Pacific Railway and a post office was established in 1874, according to the Texas State Historical Association . The town incorporated in 1887. Its early economy was largely based on cotton agriculture.
By the mid-1920s, the town had added a number of notable utilities including a telephone exchange (1900), an electric company (1914) and a water and sewage system (1923), according to TSHA. It was also more closely connected to Dallas in the mid-1920s via interurban rail and Scyene Road, later named State Highway 352.
Population growth was slow throughout much of the first half of the 20th century, but accelerated in the 1950s and beyond. The city went from less than 1,700 residents in 1950 to more than 27,500 by 1960. The growth was helped by a series of municipal annexations that saw the town grow from around one square mile to more than 20 square miles, per TSHA.
Related: Mesquite, Texas: From sleepy train depot to bustling midcentury suburb
Big Town Mall opened in Mesquite in 1959 and was later followed by Town East Mall in 1971, which was the largest shopping center in North Texas when it opened. A private airport opened in 1975 and was purchased by the city of Mesquite in 1983. Now called the Mesquite Metro Airport, the facility remains an important city asset and a key relief airport for DFW.
Mesquite grew to more than 100,000 people by 1990 and is now home to more than 150,000 residents. Other major improvements in more recent years include the inauguration of the Mesquite Arts Center in 1995 and Mesquite Freedom Park, which was dedicated in 2016 on the 15th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks.
Royce Johnson of Nemaha, NE wrestles a steer after sliding off his horse at the opening weekend of the Mesquite ProRodeo held in the Resistol Arena, Saturday, June 1, 2013. (Staff Photographer) Notable landmarks Gomez Western Wear Arena: This venue, formerly known as Mesquite Arena, is home to the Mesquite Championship Rodeo. The historic rodeo dates to 1958, according to the city, and takes place on Saturday nights in the summer. Mesquite was officially named the Rodeo Capital of Texas in 1993 by the State Legislature.
Town East Mall: When it opened in 1971, this shopping center was the largest in the D-FW area. Today, it remains a major retail hub in the eastern part of the metropolitan area.
The main entrance to Town East Mall in Mesquite near the BJ'S restaurant and brewhouse, on Dec. 26, 2020. (Ben Torres/Special Contributor) Things to do Bars and restaurants Alejandro’s Bear Cave Coffee Espadas Brazilian Steakhouse Restaurant Joe’s Pizza Mesquite BBQ Soulman's Bar-B-Que Yia Yia's House of Gyros Parks and trails Here’s a look at some notable parks and trails in Mesquite:
City Lake Park DeBusk Park and Trail Mesquite Heritage Trail Paschall Park Town East Park and Trail Valley Creek Park and Trail Westlake Park Find more here.
Shopping The Marketplace at Towne Centre Town East Mall Music director Felix Torres leads string players from the Mesquite Symphony Orchestra in a performance of Tchaikovsky’s ‘Serenade for Strings’ on March 20, 2021 in the Mesquite Arts Center. (Mesquite Symphony Orchestra) Entertainment AMC Mesquite 30 Mesquite Arts Center Mesquite Championship Rodeo A fun fact Mesquite was among the first communities in Dallas County to officially incorporate. It did so in 1887, making it only the third town to do so in the county, following Dallas and Lancaster.
